title: Father loses everything at the New Orleans race track
summary: His father started going to New Orleans races and lost the home and gambling place; Cootie refused to return from New York when asked.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And then he started going to New Orleans, to the race track.
Oh, so that's what I'm talking about when I say legitimately.
Yeah.
I see. So, how far would New Orleans be from Mobile?
90 miles.
90 miles. What would he do, drive?
Yeah. Or catch the train and go over there.
Yeah. And go down for the races.
Yeah. And that's how he got broke.
Oh. How many years did that go on?

That didn't go on many years, I don't think, because when I came to New York, it was '28, 1928. He wrote me a letter and told me he was going to sell the house, the home, if I didn't come home. So I wrote back and told him to sell it, because I wasn't coming back home. So he lost the home, lost the gambling place, lost everything.
Oh, Cootie. And he did all right with the gambling place, and it was on the horses that he lost
everything.
Yeah.
Well, why did he ask you if you were coming home? Wasn't your younger brother at home?
Yeah.
And what about the other two boys?
No.
They had moved out?
They had moved out.
I see. So he meant just for himself and the younger boy, unless you were going to come and be earning money, I guess.
Maybe so.
